newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end down in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end down in dull trade.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended down on Wednesday, dragged down by some speculative selling ahead of the close and trading was dull with the London Metal Exchange (LME) consolidating on Tuesday, traders said.
The most actively traded September 1997 contract ended at 23,920 yuan ($2,885) per tonne, losing 130 yuan. It opened at 24,000 yuan, hitting an intraday high of 24,010 and a low of 23,900.
June fell 50 yuan to 23,350, July 150 to 23,500, August 130 to 23,710, October 140 to 23,910, November 110 to 23,900 and the first traded December contract ended at 23,970.
Combined volume rose to 19,890 tonnes from 19,280.
Copper opened mixed and fell further for most of the session.
"Profit-taking from some wary retail investors dominated today's trading," one trader said. "Big speculative funds are reluctant to enter the market due to short-term market uncertainties."
"Copper producers are likely to build large short positions if the local red metal stands above the 24,000 yuan level due to lower physical prices," another trader said.
The price of physical copper is around 23,300 yuan per tonne.
Traders said they expected copper to move down if the LME cannot show strong upward momentum.
Aluminium ended mostly up. June fell 50 to 15,350 yuan per tonne, July rose 50 to 15,550 and August 10 to 15,700.
Combined volume fell to 230 tonnes from 740.
